cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul and his companions say they were torn away "in person, not in heart…" and their desire to see the Thessalonians face to face was "…even more intense." (1 Thessalonians 2:17). Far away in body, right next to them in heart, friends. That's some strong missing.

The answer is Satan. Paul writes, "…we wanted to come to you—indeed I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us." (1 Thessalonians 2:18). Paul names who was in the way, friends, and he doesn't give up on wanting to come.

The answer is the Thessalonians themselves. Paul asks, "…who is our hope, our joy, our crown of boasting, if it is not you yourselves in the presence of our Lord Jesus at His coming?" (1 Thessalonians 2:19). Then he says it plain: "You are indeed our glory and our joy." (1 Thessalonians 2:20). Not a trophy, not a building. The PEOPLE.

The word is strengthened. Paul says they sent Timothy "…to strengthen and encourage you in your faith…" (1 Thessalonians 3:2). Strengthen and encourage, friends. That's a good helper to send. Like a friend who shows up with a toolbox AND a pep talk.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…when we were with you, we kept warning you that we would suffer persecution; and as you know, it has come to pass." (1 Thessalonians 3:4). No promise of a free pass, just a warning, and he kept repeating it. Honest, straight talk from a good friend.

The word is vain. Paul fears "…that the tempter had somehow tempted you and that our labor might have been in vain." (1 Thessalonians 3:5). All that work, and he's worried about how it turned out. Anybody who's ever put hours into a batch knows that worry, friends.

The answer is good news about their faith and love. Timothy came back "…with the good news about your faith, your love, and the fond memories you have preserved…" (1 Thessalonians 3:6). Faith and love, both on the list, friends. That's the report Paul was hoping for, I bet.

The answer is True. Timothy returned with news of the Thessalonians "…longing to see us just as we long to see you." (1 Thessalonians 3:6). The missing goes both ways, friends. Nobody's waiting alone at the window.

The word is firm. Paul says, "For now we can go on living, as long as you are standing firm in the Lord." (1 Thessalonians 3:8). Timothy had just come back with good news about their faith, and Paul says that reassured them (1 Thessalonians 3:6-7). Standing firm shows how much he cares about them.

The answer is to supply what is lacking in their faith. Paul says they pray "Night and day…" and "most earnestly" to see them face to face "…and supply what is lacking in your faith." (1 Thessalonians 3:10). They want to fill in what's missing, friends. A good teacher always has more to share.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "…may the Lord cause you to increase and overflow with love for one another and for everyone else, just as our love for you overflows…" (1 Thessalonians 3:12). "…for one another and for everyone else…" Overflowing means it doesn't stop at the edge of the cup, friends.

The answer is blameless and holy hearts when Jesus comes. Paul writes, "…so that He may establish your hearts in blamelessness and holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints." (1 Thessalonians 3:13). It's a prayer about hearts being established and ready for that day, friends. It's exactly why my ovens stay warm.
